title: RAW looks
objective: Start new RAW photos from a Luxforge look instead of the bare neutral development: the Standard look by default (phase 1), and Match camera, fitted per photo to its embedded camera preview, as a preference (phase 2), on one recipe layer, payload and set of GPU units.
context_summary: Planned from docs/design/raw-looks.md, the contract every task follows. The owner decided on 2026-10-05 that new RAW photos start from a Luxforge look, that matching the camera preview is a setting, and that Standard is built first, and accepted the design's defaults the same day. Phase 1 is TASK-001 to TASK-005 and is deliverable on its own; phase 2 is TASK-006 to TASK-008; TASK-009 measures once at the end. The look is a colour-stage layer at order 3 (after Basic, before the Tone curve), written into a new RAW photograph's Original from the raw_look preference, with resolved knots stored in every payload. It reuses the Tone curve's interpolant with a new tail policy and Basic's Oklab chroma unit where exact, and adds a path-to-white unit; every unit has a CPU unit checked exactly against an f64 reference fixture and a WGSL program qualified within the GPU tolerance. The GPU-first integration is in flight: GPU_PROGRAMS, the GPU qualification step list, the conformance list and the descriptor snapshot are regenerated after any rebase, never hand-merged. Supplied RAW files come from the owner's private manifest; none enter the repository. Decisions: docs/decisions.md.

tasks.description: Freeze the look numerics and choose the Standard look: the f64 reference for the tone, chroma, path-to-white and amount units, the study over the corpus, the oracle fixture and the owner's contact-sheet review.
extra_context: Create crates/luxforge-reference/src/look.rs beside curve.rs, calling crate::tone::luminance, crate::srgb's extended transfer and the curve reference's interpolant construction rather than restating them; the look tail policy (linear continuation of the first segment below 0, hold at the last knot above x_max) is new and the Tone curve's unit-slope tails are untouched.

Units in order: tone (encoded-luminance PCHIP over at most 24 knots on [0, x_max], x_max = encode(2^H), floor-subtracted luminance-ratio reconstruction), uniform Oklab chroma gain at constant lightness and hue, path to white above a knee k (closed form or a fixed number of bisection steps, chosen here so the GPU cost is fixed), amount blend out = in + a(look(in) - in) with amount 0-200.

Standard is chosen by measurement: histogram-match each corpus file's as-shot development to its largest embedded JPEG (the same matching the camera fit will use, here as an instrument in the study only) and set the Standard's lift and midtone slope near the corpus median; recorded defaults before measuring are +0.5 EV lift, log-logistic midtone slope about 1.5, H = +1 EV, chroma 1.10-1.20. Use the CC0 corpus and the owner's private RAW manifest; no RAW enters the repository.

Write a contact sheet of about 24 corpus frames (Neutral, Standard, camera preview side by side) to a temp directory for the owner. The numbers freeze only after the owner has reviewed it; record the chosen values and the figures in the design.

Study tests over named and seeded random inputs: monotone tone on an extended ramp including negative and above-white luminance; greys stay grey; Oklab hue kept through tone and chroma; no channel clips at or below sensor white at amount 100; path to white never increases chroma and leaves colours below the knee unchanged; finite on extreme inputs; amount 0 is the identity and amount 100 the look; a regenerable oracle fixture of cases with their expected outputs.

Done 2026-10-05; the owner approved the contact sheets the same day: the reference (src/look.rs), the corpus export (crates/luxforge-raw/tests/look_corpus.rs), the study and fixture (fixtures/look/look-cases.json); the frozen Standard (lift +1.15 EV, contrast 1.6, headroom 1.5 EV, chroma 1.2, knee 0.8) and its figures are in the design. The chroma unit is Basic's Saturation exactly; the path to white is a closed form mixing toward the colour's own luminance grey.

tasks.description: Make the shared pieces the look unit needs: the Tone curve's interpolant reusable by another module with the look's tails, and the core's Oklab conversions reachable from it, leaving the Tone curve's unit, program and outputs unchanged.
extra_context: modules/curve/unit.rs keeps Interpolant pub(super); widen it to pub(crate) and give it a tail policy: the Tone curve's (unit-slope tails outside [0, 1], flat holds) or the look's (the first segment continued linearly below 0, the last value held at and above x_max, knots spanning [0, x_max] with x_max above 1). The Tone curve's ToneCurve unit, its describe string, its GPU program and words are untouched, and its fixture and GPU qualification pass unchanged.

crate::colour's to_oklab and from_oklab are pub(crate) already; the look unit uses them directly. Basic's ColourAdjust unit is not reused: the look's chroma step is a uniform gain inside the fused look unit.
This task and the look module are built together, by one change: the path-to-white and amount steps live in the fused look unit, whose GPU qualification runs through a look layer.

tasks.description: Build the luxforge.look module: descriptor, payload, set-look, reset-look, sample-look, compilation to units, history labels, recipe description and conformance.
extra_context: The look compiles to one fused pointwise unit (tone, chroma, path to white, amount) with one WGSL program lf_look_look listed in GPU_PROGRAMS between COLOUR_ADJUST_PROGRAM and TONE_CURVE_PROGRAM; see the design's 'GPU and reference'. Its CPU unit is checked against fixtures/look/look-cases.json at every step, and its program by a gpu_colour_look_meets_the_pointwise_limits qualification in crates/luxforge-app/src/app/gpu_colour_tests.rs.

Create crates/luxforge-core/src/modules/look/ (mod.rs, standard.rs holding the frozen Standard knots and chroma, unit wiring). EffectDescriptor: stage Color, order 3, single, sources [Raw], not maskable. Register it after Basic and before Curve in modules/registry/mod.rs.

Payload {look, amount, tone, chroma, fit}; neutral payload {look: neutral}. set-look {look?, amount?} resolves standard to the current Standard's knots and chroma; look: camera is refused with a pointer to match-camera-look (phase 2). reset-look returns to Standard. Neutral and amount 0 compile to no unit. If the field-patch contract cannot carry the resolved tone, chroma and fit fields, implement the actions directly as Lens does.
Neutrality per the recorded default: the band dot is lit only when the look is not the current Standard at amount 100.

query.sample-look answers 257 samples over [0, x_max] and the chroma gain without reading pixels; recipe.describe reports look, amount, chroma, knot count and fit. Labels: Look Standard, Look Neutral, Look amount N, Reset Look.
Presets: not presettable. Update the Lightroom CameraProfile reason text in presets/mapping.rs and docs/design/presets.md to "Luxforge's looks are its own".
Regenerate the builtin descriptor snapshot and add the module to the conformance KNOWN list.

tasks.description: Start new RAW photos from the preferred look: the ToolModule::original hook, the raw_look preference (standard or neutral) in the core, API and General tab, and the look in a new RAW photograph's Original.
extra_context: Add ToolModule::original(&self, context) -> Option<layer>, asked in registry order by EditorService::new_photograph (editor/source.rs) for a new photograph's Original from its kind, metadata and the preferences; the look module returns its payload for standard and nothing for neutral. JPEG photographs get no look. seed.rs mirrors new_photograph.

Preference raw_look: an enum like CanvasBackground in preferences.rs (ALL, as_str, parse, default standard), announced as a General row, pushed into EditorService as auto_lens_profile is (api/owner.rs at owner start and in preferences_set). Desktop: a GeneralPreference variant after the lens row, a choice control, title Starting look for new RAW photos.

Existing photos and their recipes are never rewritten. Tests that assert a bare neutral RAW Original set raw_look to neutral or update their expectations from the reference; fixtures are regenerated, never hand-edited.
pick.develop must stay metadata-only: no pixel or file read is added by the hook.

tasks.description: Freeze the camera fit: the reference fitter, its study over the corpus and its fixture.
extra_context: In crates/luxforge-reference/src/look.rs: exclusion of clipped and crushed preview pixels and non-finite development pixels; 1024-bin encoded-luminance histograms; the monotone quantile map at fixed quantiles with slope floor and cap; the join to the Standard shoulder above the highest confident quantile; the median Oklab chroma ratio on mid-lightness chromatic pixels, clamped to 0.7-1.6; monochrome-preview detection keeping chroma 1.0; refusal below 10% usable pixels.
Preview colour: sRGB or untagged as sRGB, and Adobe RGB by ICC profile or EXIF colour space, converted to linear sRGB; anything else refused with its reason.

Study figures per camera over the CC0 corpus and the owner manifest: fit success rate, median luminance error against the preview, chroma gain spread, refusals and their reasons. No pixel equivalence with any camera is claimed.

tasks.description: Fit camera looks in the core off the owner: the preview read and decode, the cached fit per source, the first-open data hook, edit.match-camera-look through the off-owner pixel-read path, and announced first-open entries.
extra_context: The fit reads the original's largest embedded JPEG through EmbeddedPreviews (prepare_bytes already holds the file's bytes before RawPrepared::decode), cut at its last EOI as previews/region.rs does, decoded at a DCT scale through luxforge-jpeg, and the as-shot development downscaled to at most 1024 px. Cache one fit per source identity beside the prepared source.

Extend first open: a hook run on the source worker where await_first_open runs, given the prepared development and the original's bytes, returning opaque data the module's first_open reads from its context. With raw_look camera the Original still holds Standard (TASK-004) and first open commits Look Match camera by the system actor; a refused fit is reported in the preparation's first_open list and the photo stays at revision 0.

edit.match-camera-look takes no parameters and defers its fit as a new read kind of the Detail design's off-owner pixel-read path, keyed by source identity and development, under MAX_PIXEL_READ_ROUNDS and the point queue capacity; refused with unavailable: and the reason when there is no usable preview.

Announce committed first-open entries to the preview lane as edits are announced (api/owner.rs source_complete), so tiles rendered from the Original re-render; this also covers the lens entry. Confirm the gap with a failing test first.

Add the ignored owner test owner_raw_camera_look beside the existing owner RAW tests: it fits the supplied Z6, X100VI and Air 2S files and checks the first-open entry, the cached fit and the reference agreement.
